what: kè đường Hạ Long: a piece of 2 m of the sloped sea wall of concrete panels of Hạ Long, from the outer edge of the walk down to the rocks at the water
uses: Plan 0026, R4, R6, Q12: under the walk of the sea of Hạ Long (sea_walls of data/showcase/bai_truoc.json): the game puts the pieces one after another along the line, the port end of a piece on the port start of the next, the top edge (the origin) at the outer edge of the walk under the parapet, the slope down to +y. The game scales each piece in height to the drop at its place (the height of the walk less the height of the ground 7 m past the parapet: 0.3 m to 14 m along the line); the run stays 7.0 m. There is no walk at the level of the sand along Hạ Long.

sources.author: Venanzio_KH (Flickr)
sources.shows: The sea wall of Hạ Long from its foot, to the north: the sloped face of concrete panels with joints down the slope about 2 m apart, rust brown and dark stains on its lower part, grey and brown rocks of 0.5 m to 0.8 m at the water, the parapet and the road on top, lamp posts of four globes, the hotel with the letters HA LONG HOTEL, the terminal of Cầu Đá.

sources.author: Venanzio_KH (Flickr)
sources.shows: Hạ Long between Bãi Trước and Cầu Đá: the walk of grey and dark tiles with a low parapet of plain concrete with a round top, the steep slope of concrete down to rocks, a lamp post of four white globes, a bench, houses under Núi Nhỏ.

sources.author: trungydang
sources.shows: The sea wall of Hạ Long to the north: a smooth sloped face of concrete from the parapet down to rocks at the water, the parapet of rough stone (before its cladding of granite), the walk with lamp posts of white globes, the road, hotels and Bãi Trước far away.

sources.author: Thành Duy / VnExpress
sources.shows: From a drone over the sea: the light sloped sea wall of Hạ Long from the south end of Bãi Trước to the jetty of Cầu Đá, flat rocks at the foot of the slope, the boats of the bay; no walk at the level of the sand.

length.source: A piece of the row, one panel wide. Photo 0: the joints of the panels go down the slope, about as far apart as the parapet is long between two lamp posts divided by five: about 2 m.

height.source: The drop: the height of the walk less the height of the ground of the game 7 m past the parapet (report 0026, Q17). I measured it along the line of the sea wall of Hạ Long: 0.3 m to 14 m, median 3.3 m. The model has the median; the game scales each piece in height to the drop at its place.

run.source: Photo 0 (2021-05-10): the camera is level (the horizon is a straight row of the photo, 390 px of 768 px), and the lines of the wall meet at 632 px on the horizon. Four long joints of the panels go down the slope in the middle of the photo (at 630 px to 880 px across and 502 px to 600 px down). With these, the slope is 23 to 27 degrees for a lens of 580 px to 900 px: the run is 2.0 to 2.4 times the drop, 2.1 in the mean. 2.1 × 3.3 m: 6.9 m; 7.0 m. In photos 0 and 1 the top of the face curves up to the foot of the parapet; the model has one plain slope.

rock.source: Photo 0: the rocks at the water are about a third of a panel (2 m): 0.5 m to 0.8 m, blocks with round edges.

toe.source: estimate (no source): two rows of rocks in front of the foot (photos 0 and 3 show rocks at the foot).

colors.value: concrete #b5ada0, rust brown stains #7d5f45 on the lower third and dark wet stains #4f4a42 at the foot, rocks #5f5a52 to #7a7065
colors.source: Photo 0 (2021): light grey concrete with rust brown and dark stains near the foot, grey and brown rocks; photo 2 (2014) shows the same face.

looks.seen: Next to photos 0 and 2: the slope from the top edge down to the foot and the light concrete are as in the photos. The stains on the lower part hardly show (in photos 0 and 2 the lower third is rust brown and dark). The rocks are too small, too round and too few: in photo 0 they are angular blocks of 0.5 m to 0.8 m in a band at the foot, some on the slope.
looks.changed: Stronger stains (the lower third, opacity 0.65) and a dark wet band at the foot; eight rocks of 0.7 m as blocks with round edges at a slant, one on the slope.

looks.seen: Next to photos 0 and 2: the rocks are now angular blocks in a band at the foot, one on the slope, as in photo 0. The rust brown of the lower third is still weaker than in photo 2 (2014) and photo 0 (2021).
looks.changed: The stains to #7d5f45 with an opacity of 0.8.

looks.seen: Next to photos 0 and 2: the lower third of the slope is now rust brown, and a dark band is at the foot, as in the photos; the upper part is the light concrete. The rocks are angular blocks.
The mid level of the last blueprint: the same as the look before.

Next to photos 0 and 2: the light concrete with the rust brown lower third and the dark foot, angular rocks at the foot, a thin joint down the slope at the start of the piece. In photo 0 the rocks are more and in a wider band, and the panels have more stains and lines of water.

Next to photos 0 and 1 (2021) and photo 2 (2014): a long plain slope of 25 degrees from the top edge down 3.3 m over 7.0 m, light concrete with the rust brown lower third and a dark foot, and angular rocks at the foot, as the face of photo 0. The old order had a drop of 4.0 m over 6.0 m (34 degrees): the joints of the panels in photo 0 give 23 to 27 degrees. Still different: the rocks are a small group at the foot of the piece, and in photo 0 they are a wide band of many rocks; the face has no joints of panels at this level; the top of the face does not curve up to the parapet as in photos 0 and 1.
looks.changed: Nothing at the mid level. Next: the near level.

looks.seen: Not built. The factory stopped at the near level of this order two times (HTTP 503: the order needs more memory than the edge has): the piece is now 7.0 m deep and 3.3 m high with cells of 0.04 m. The near level of the old order (2.0 m by 6.0 m by 4.0 m) built.
looks.changed: Nothing. The cells are in the blueprint ke_bien.json, and a change of the blueprint changes each order of its family, so I did not change them. The near level needs the job "Models of World" (mix world.order).

looks.seen: Report 0026, Q25: the files of the lock of World e8754d6 (build/look/ke_ha_long_mid.png). The sloped sea wall of concrete panels with the rocks at its foot, as in photo 0.
Report 0026, Q25: the files of the lock of World e8754d6 (build/look/ke_ha_long_far.png). The same slope, the rocks as a few blocks.

status_note: Source (report 0026, Q17). Rule 2: photos 0 and 1 (2021-05-10) show the sloped face of concrete panels and the rocks at its foot; photo 2 (2014-04-05) shows the same face, so it was the look in 2019 (rule 1). The drop comes from the ground of the game, and the run from photo 0. The toe of rocks is an estimate (no source). On 2026-11-17 the image of photo 3 (VnExpress) did not open (HTTP 401), so I did not use it.
